evidence_notes: Formatting and trailing-comma cleanup reflects a repository convention issue.

In the 2025-02-11 origin patch, getFilenamesInDir returns from inside the try/catch before reaching the existing migration-guide nesting logic, so migration documents can no longer be emitted as children. Commit 53bb1287 on 2025-04-17 removes those early returns, retains content-title fallback handling, and restores the migration-guide child construction. No linked issue, CI failure, test, or user report is supplied.

The origin sidebar still contains the config-based connector tutorial category. Commit 46359769 on 2025-03-31 hard-deprecates the connector generator script and deletes that tutorial category from docusaurus/sidebars.js; the supplied evidence shows a later repository-maintenance/deletion change rather than an origin-time failure or explicit report.

At origin, MongoDbDebeziumPropertiesManager changed CDC setup to use client-level database.include.list handling and removed capture.target. Repair commit 430c404049859324e7865b33f5c2fe20976f0124 explicitly adds database-scoped capture.scope/capture.target handling for a single database and updates tests to mock MongoClient.getDatabase(...).watch(...), stating that the change allows read permission for single-database use. No issue, CI failure, or user report is supplied.

The origin implementation of MongoDbDebeziumStateUtil validates resume tokens with a newly constructed MongoDB change-stream pipeline, while the repair commit d0910bdedf9cb8f7ef120e0d3061f0f439b92242 replaces that logic with Debezium's change-stream machinery and documents that validation must use the same pipeline as Debezium. The supplied evidence contains no explicit failure, issue, CI result, or user report.

The origin changes offset state handling from database-name identifiers to connection-string-based identifiers but retains generic normalization and migration behavior; its test expects a generic server-id normalization. Repair commit 8e17db88ef84741289619c93968875d6816f839c removes the database-name fallback migration, uses normalizeToDebeziumFormat for connection strings, and changes the test to assert the canonical connection-string format. No explicit issue, CI failure, or user report is supplied.

At origin merge (2025-06-04), Card.jsx replaced the native <a href={href}> with a <button onClick={() => window.location.href = href} role="link">, preserving ordinary navigation but not the browser anchor interaction contract. The repair commit (2026-04-28) restored <a href={href}> specifically to support cmd+click. No linked issue, CI, test, or explicit user report establishes how the gap was exposed, so the pathway is uncertain.

The origin PR introduced the V2 write operation and check-operation bean, plus explicit test-container shutdown. Repair commit 667ab295516efda35296213907618bc0eb33354f updates to CDK 0.2.0, deletes WriteOperationV2.kt, removes the check-operation bean, and removes PostgresCheckTest.stopContainer() because parallel tests may still need the container. No linked issue or failure evidence is supplied.

At origin, PostgresAirbyteClient.countTable() and generation-ID retrieval catch every Exception and interpret it as a missing table. Repair commit ba3c131443c109a0b6b5432a3ec244b01b5cd113 limits that behavior to SQLSTATE 42P01/3F000, rethrows other errors, and adds tests for connection failures and wrapped missing-table exceptions. No issue, CI failure, or user report is supplied; the observable route is test expansion.

The origin implementation generated ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN statements through PostgresDirectLoadSqlGenerator.matchSchemas() and passed deleted columns from PostgresAirbyteClient. Repair commit 2ddb22251db6be1155c2723c8a9e6c7c28087d60 removes that logic, removes the corresponding unit test, and sets ColumnDropBehavior.RETAIN in both acceptance tests, indicating a later schema-evolution contract/requirement change. No linked issue or explicit failure evidence is supplied.
The bespoke PostgreSQL schema utilities were consolidated into the established CDK utility pattern; this is primarily structural cohesion.

The origin SQL generator derived primary-key and cursor indexes from mapped user columns, while PostgresColumnUtils tests explicitly expected those columns to be absent in legacy raw-table mode. Commit 88209fa39f0a77f9fbbd94eb67d61a53866614c moved the raw-mode check into index creation and removed the obsolete raw-mode utility tests. The supplied repair is a refactor/test cleanup, with no explicit failure or issue evidence.

At origin, PostgresValueCoercer handled NUL characters in scalar strings but did not sanitize nested object/array values before JSON serialization. Commit a4ff7ba501a0ee3db488b1685d2f546a8c91d397 added recursive NUL stripping in production code plus unit and acceptance tests for nested values and keys. No linked issue, explicit failure report, or CI evidence is supplied, so this is test expansion/internal maintenance.

At origin, PostgresAirbyteClient passed shouldRecreatePrimaryKeyIndex(...) and shouldRecreateCursorIndex(...) directly to matchSchemas. The repair adds a raw-tables-mode guard because primary-key and cursor columns are stored in _airbyte_data JSONB and do not exist as physical columns. No issue, CI, test, or explicit failure evidence identifies how the defect was exposed.

Origin PR migrated PostgresWriter from TableCatalog to DestinationCatalog and retained namespace creation only for final table names. Repair commit 1bfa189f added deduplicated namespace creation for temp-table namespaces and internalTableSchema, indicating those setup obligations were omitted during the origin migration. No linked issue, failure report, CI evidence, or explicit user report was supplied; exposure is shown through the later schema-utility refactor.

At origin, PostgresAirbyteClient passed generated deleted columns to schema matching and applyChangeset, while the generic schema-evolution test explicitly covered dropping columns. Commit 2ddb2225 removed DROP handling from both paths and changed PostgresTableSchemaEvolutionTest to override columnDropBehavior as RETAIN. No issue, failure, or CI evidence was supplied.

At origin, PostgresWriter.setup created namespaces only for final table names, although createStreamLoader already used a tempTableName. Commit 1bfa189f added namespace creation for temp-table namespaces and the configured internal table schema, while also refactoring PostgresAirbyteClient to the CDK schema-utility pattern. The later production setup change made the missing namespace obligation observable; no explicit issue or failure was supplied.

The origin PostgresRawDataDumper built the reverse column mapping and typed reconstruction from stream.schema/ObjectType. Commit ffcfbcd4 changed both to use stream.tableSchema.columnSchema.inputSchema, indicating the dumper had assumed the source schema was equivalent to the canonical mapped input schema. No explicit issue, failure, or CI evidence was supplied.

At origin, PostgresDirectLoadSqlGenerator.matchSchemas accepted columnsToRemove and emitted ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN statements, with a corresponding removal test. The 2026-08-05 repair removed the columnsToRemove parameter, DROP logic, and removal test, indicating the origin assumed removed stream columns should be physically dropped but that schema-evolution contract was later corrected. No issue, CI, test failure, or user report is supplied; exposure is therefore maintenance/deletion-driven (P-C).

Origin PR changed NumberType to DecimalType and removed DECIMAL from unsupported types, assuming Iceberg decimal identifiers and schema evolution were valid; it added decimal comparison and widening logic. The PR explicitly cites issue #63359 and the failure caused by unusable numeric primary-key identifiers. Repair commit 419b0a7efd2b65b7c6798df0ecec971f4c17db90 reinstates DECIMAL as unsupported, removes decimal widening/comparison support, and changes PK NumberType handling to StringType, indicating the original contract assumption was corrected.

At origin, SnowflakeFieldTypes.kt truncated nanoseconds downward to microseconds for values used by incremental cursors, implicitly assuming precision reduction was safe. The 2026-08-13 repair changes both accessors to round up, stating that reducing a cursor bound can make it compare below a row and cause silent record loss. The repair commit explicitly names silent record loss (#82705), but no issue or CI evidence is supplied to distinguish an explicit failure report from another exposure route.

Origin test_source.py only parsed manifest.yaml and asserted configured actions; the PR explicitly described it as a static YAML validation rather than a runtime behavior test. Repair commit f1c2bcbc replaced that test with runtime instantiation checks for all streams and fixed use of the error_handler key, exposing that the custom handler was not being instantiated.

The origin PR added the Community help article on 2025-04-07. The next-day repair commit is titled “Make community chat feature opt-in by default” and updates the article’s enablement and navigation instructions, including changing “Communities” to “Community,” removing the prior access flow, and revising feature guidance. This indicates the documented obligation became applicable after the Community interface/behavior evolved; the response was documentation correction.

Origin PR added product_review_response routes in existing route sections but not the custom-domain route scope. Repair commit 9f1de3e12306c656651bb380365d8bbf1c5d5884, titled 'Fix reviews not loading on custom domains', adds the review routes there; issue ref 4718 is present. The repair corrects the routing/interface contract for that scope.

At origin merge (2025-07-02), the limit was implemented directly as a Link validation with no bypass or exemption path. The later production repair, fae3183ccc455b7a6786aac2f0ff39d8251150ec (2025-08-08), extracts the behavior into Product::CreationLimit and is explicitly titled “with bypass & exemption support”; it removes the original validation and its specs. No issue, CI failure, or user report is supplied, so the later production-code/requirement evolution is the identifiable exposure route.

Repair commit a7c3a406 adds an iteration over CROSS_BORDER_PAYOUTS_COUNTRIES asserting each country returns a non-nil minimum, and removes the broad zero-value expectations.
The origin logic excluded chargebacks from the sale report; later reporting distinguishes sale date from chargeback event date.

Commit 37c3264 (2026-07-17), referencing issue #5890, changed the report contract to retain the sale by purchase date and add a negative refund entry by refund date; specs were updated accordingly.
The job duplicated a shared Indian-state list and validation instead of using the common compliance utility.

The initial test covered only scheduled no-argument execution; later-added replay and explicit-argument paths were not covered.

The repair title explicitly identifies exclusion of the validation in the test environment; no linked issue, CI failure, or user report is supplied.

Repair commit fae3183ccc455b7a6786aac2f0ff39d8251150ec removes the daily-limit spec block while extracting the limit with bypass and exemption support; no issue, failure, CI, or user report is supplied, so exposure is attributable to refactoring/deletion maintenance.

The later commit e63ee60d (2026-04-27), titled 'Fix flaky CI tests: timing, stale elements, and browser dialog handling', changed the alert error handling and added a retry sleep, indicating CI exposed the unresolved timing obligation.

The later structured-comments API and limit changed the interface and made the earlier unbounded handling relevant.

Repair commit bccc1f3e8388 added the still-applicable fee as a separate statement. No issue, CI, test, or explicit failure triggered the repair; it was a later documentation correction.

Origin controller uses @Roles but its @UseGuards list omits RolesGuard, despite the PR claiming authentication and authorization guards. Commit 0f0c2b8 adds the RolesGuard import and decorator entry; no linked issue, CI failure, or user report is supplied, so exposure is internal maintenance.

Origin query DTO transforms ISO-8601 strings into Date values and validates both IsISO8601 and IsDate, while the repository and service APIs likewise use Date types. Commit 43a6663 removes the Date transformation and IsDate checks and changes all affected option types to string, correcting the validation/downstream contract. No issue, CI, or explicit failure evidence is supplied.

Origin E2E cleanup deletes related records with broad or inconsistent ordering and does not delete the created user. Commit 21d6bf1 relocates cleanup to after the tests, deletes each response explicitly, adds user cleanup, and is titled as fixing flaky tests. The supplied evidence contains no separate CI failure or issue beyond this test-maintenance repair.

The origin DateRangeFilter used a fixed endOfDay option and emitted raw ISO timestamps. The 2025-09-18 repair, titled 'allow to choose dateTarget for /insights', added timezone-aware timestamp conversion, preserveLocalTime handling, and dateTarget-related behavior. The origin PR explicitly describes an existing mobile-display failure: event titles/subtitles were hidden by `hidden` and `md:block` classes in `ShellMainAppDir.tsx`. The origin patch removes those classes to satisfy mobile visibility. Commit `254a2e310baa9ed3503c1fd71834e156eeca781d` later reverts those changes, restoring the responsive display contract; no linked issue or detailed reason for the revert is supplied.

Origin packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots/util.ts imported getPeriodStartDatesBetween from getUserAvailability while the availability module depended on slots utilities, creating a circular dependency. Commit badd0de33c27 extracted getPeriodStartDatesBetween to intervalLimits/utils and replaced the in-class implementation/import path.

Origin getUserAvailability.ts awaited getBusyTimesFromLimits and getBusyTimesFromTeamLimits sequentially even though both computations were independent. Commit a06b2009 changed both to promises and awaited them with Promise.all to improve performance.

Origin slots/util.ts reconstructed each global busy time with getUnitFromBusyTime and LimitManager.addBusyTime before applying it to per-user managers. Repair 601df7f replaced that reconstruction with LimitManager.mergeBusyTimes, preserving the global manager's existing busy-map entries; the commit states that slots could remain available after team booking limits were exceeded.

Origin slots/util.ts performed getTotalBookingDuration work inside the per-user limit-processing path, leaving repeated yearly duration queries. Commit f883dee084 added yearlyDurationTotals prefetching and reused the totals during per-user processing to avoid N+1 queries.

Origin util.ts directly imported getBusyTimesForLimitChecks and getStartEndDateforLimitCheck. The repair changed these calls to dependencies.busyTimesService and added busyTimesService to IAvailableSlotsService; the repair diff identifies the prior direct call with a TODO to add dependency injection.

Origin PR added repeated inline booking-period date comparisons and busy-time unit calculation in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots/util.ts. Repair commit cfc9f0bfc322fb45d4ae4e7d3344b25ed5906c38 replaced these duplicates with shared isBookingWithinPeriod and getUnitFromBusyTime helpers; no issue, failure, CI, or user report is supplied.
The same query-condition implementation was duplicated in the router and later removed in favor of the shared implementation.
The E2E test clicked delete without response synchronization and used an unqualified locator.

The test used broad page-level text assertions instead of locating the expected member-table column.

Origin filter-segment.e2e.ts used unqualified user-list-data-table locators and retained a locator across navigation. Repair c2b7dcb900130eb8928d36959b535174fb8cf831 uses first() consistently and redefines the table locator after navigation, indicating duplicated/changed page structure handled as test maintenance without a linked issue.

At origin, scanWorkflowBody marked all workflow steps verified when IFFY_API_KEY was absent and also marked whitelisted users' spam steps verified after logging them. The 2025-05-21 repair removed the no-key auto-verification path and restructured verification/spam handling, indicating the origin implementation bypassed required validation behavior. No linked issue, CI failure, test, or explicit user report distinguishes the exposure route.

Origin selectedCalendar.ts used @ts-ignore with an eslint suppression because the author could not make @ts-expect-error work consistently across CI cases. Repair commit 92d2b599 states that Biome lint errors required replacing @ts-ignore with @ts-expect-error, changing only the suppression style in both watchAttempts and unwatchAttempts queries.

Commit 22663014697b33a5b34bff240bd929d325aaf13b added waitFor() before the click in apps/web/playwright/filter-helpers.ts. No issue, CI failure, or explicit user report is supplied; this is internal E2E-helper maintenance.

The origin E2E tests used broad page.getByText(...) assertions for values expected in a specific table column. No linked issue, CI failure, or explicit report is supplied; the change is test-oracle/internal maintenance.

At origin, filterRedundantDateRanges used a nested scan over sortedRanges for every range, yielding O(n²) behavior despite the PR's stated goal of improving performance for large dateRanges arrays. Commit 93e2426 replaced the all-pairs scan with an interval tree and documented O(n log n) worst-case complexity. No supplied later failure, issue, CI, test, or static-analysis evidence establishes a P-A trigger; the repair is internal performance maintenance/refactoring.

At origin, packages/lib/slots.ts stored slot boundaries as string keys and reconstructed each key with dayjs(t) before sorting and comparison. Repair ac117a14 changed the map keys to numeric timestamps and compared numbers directly, creating Dayjs objects only when needed; the repair title identifies this as faster logic by preventing instanceof Dayjs. No linked issue, failure report, CI result, or test failure was supplied, so exposure is internal performance maintenance (P-C).

No linked issue, CI failure, test failure, or explicit later report is supplied, so the exposure is evidenced only by internal maintenance/reversion.
Date-range selection behavior was embedded in complex branching and later extracted into a cohesive helper.

The worker directly instantiated a service and bypassed NestJS dependency wiring.
The E2E test reused one browser session across users and relied on an arbitrary fixed delay.

Commit e4eeb11a (2025-06-30) changed the guard to exclude forced reschedules, correcting that control-flow contract.

The supplied origin patch does not establish that this later past-booking obligation applied at the 2025-06-07 merge.
